entities.summary:
Bonagratia of Bergamo (active 1300s) was a Franciscan canonist who played a pivotal role in the 'poverty of Christ' controversy, a theological debate that centered on the relationship between material wealth and spiritual poverty. 


 As a trained canonist, Bonagratia supported Michael of Cesena against Pope John XXII, who had taken a hardline stance against the Franciscan Order's minimalist approach to wealth. 


 The controversy, which lasted for several decades, had significant repercussions for the Catholic Church and the broader Christian world. 


 Bonagratia's stance on the matter reflects the complexities of his time, when the intersection of theology, politics, and economics was a dominant theme in European society.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bonagratia of Bergamo played a pivotal role in the 'poverty of Christ' controversy, a theological debate that centered on the relationship between material wealth and spiritual poverty. The controversy had significant repercussions for the Catholic Church and the broader Christian world, contributing to a reevaluation of the role of wealth in the Christian life.
